thread:
maria: quick share — ran the nightly allocator+kernel change (kernel-selector v3) against the 2k-concurrent decode workload and saw ~18% OOM spike on medium-length requests at 95th p99.
jun: ugh, can you paste the perf traces? is this hitting KV-prefill or decode path?
maria: traces point to fragmentation after prefill demotions. Looks like we demote slots too aggressively when switching kernels which leaves many tiny free fragments that later fail big prefill allocations — repro in perf lab.
ryan: do we have a concrete repro script? I can try on dedicated pool.
maria: yes, ran: ```./bench/run.sh --workload decode-heavy --concurrency 2000 --seed 42 --kv-prefill=on --kernel-select=v3``` output attached below.
perf-bot: bench run finished: 2000 req/s peak, avg latency 48ms, p99 210ms, OOMs: 37
maria: pprof snapshot (heap by size): ```heap: total 6.8G
  slab_512: 2.1G (many fragments)
  slab_8k: 3.9G
  workspace_active: 0.8G
  free_fragments: 48M (count: 72k)``` this suggests many small fragments.
jun: interesting — the kernel switch reduced per-request workspace but increased demotion churn. We might need a size-aware demotion threshold rather than count-based.
ryan: proposal: introduce a soft per-request KV reserve (e.g., reserve 8k per active request) + a size-aware demote that coalesces contiguous free slots before returning to global free list. branch: fix/size-aware-demote
maria: I prototyped a cheap coalesce pass on demote and ran the same bench. Results: OOMs down to 3, p99 down 15%.
sre-ops: nice. any impact on tail latency for tiny requests? we don't want extra latency in happy path.
maria: coalesce pass is async (background) on demote path; immediate demote still returns small fragments but they get merged within 50–200ms. Tiny request latency unchanged in microbench.
jun: another angle: switch prefill to try small-object packing when free_fragments > threshold. I think we should combine both: soft reserve + async coalesce + prefill packing.
ryan: agree. Also add a heuristic to avoid kernel-switch-triggered demote during high concurrency — maybe add hysteresis so we don't flip kernels a lot.
maria: here's a short patch snippet i used: ```diff
- if (prefill_demote_count > 4) demote();
+ if (prefill_demote_count > 4 && !high_concurrency()) demote();
+ // async coalesce launched for demoted ranges
``` tested with kernel hysteresis + soft reserve (8k/request) + async coalesce: OOMs -> 0 in 10 runs.
perf-bot: regression test: memory-bandwidth delta +1.2% (acceptable), cpu overhead +0.3%.
ryan: can you open a PR and add the bench in perf-suite? then we can run on dedicated and a/b roll.
maria: opened PR #4123, added perf graphs and flame with before/after. Link: https://git.redwood/reviews/4123
jun: add a config flag for rollout (kv.size_aware_demote=true) so we can ramp in Dedicated.
sre-ops: please also add alert if OOM increases by >5 in 1h after rollout — we'll watch production.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
ryan: tagging @jun for kernel selection heuristics follow-up.
jun: will write a spec for kernel hysteresis thresholds. planning to keep default conservative.
maria: last note — this only impacted workloads with mixed prefill/decode ratios. pure decode or pure prefill didn't regress. put that in the PR notes.
perf-bot: CI: perf-suite run queued on dedicated cluster — will post results here when done.
